program.name: Spark-DO
program.headline: Real estate development and construction management apprenticeship
program.lede: Four years at 3F Construction: six months of field support, 30 months of coursework that is put to use on live jobs, and a final year running a project as its superintendent.
program.description: A four-year apprenticeship in real estate development and construction management at 3F Construction: field work, applied coursework and a capstone year.
program.title: Real estate development and construction management apprenticeship | Spark-DO

phases.title: Field support
study: Supports a field superintendent on 3F Construction jobs
Joins every project call, including owner-architect-contractor (OAC) meetings and internal coordination calls
Helps coordinate between the field and the office
Takes on field assignments that mean reviewing drawings and coordinating with subcontractors and the project management team
phases.milestone: Shows the ability to work hard and quickly on field assignments.

phases.title: Project management
phases.split: 8 hours of coursework and 2 applying it on a live company job
study: Columbia University's Construction Management specialization on Coursera: five courses, about 110 hours by Coursera's estimate
Each course is applied to one active job: reading the schedule, tracking a budget line, sitting in on owner and subcontractor meetings
phases.milestone: Earns the certificate, then builds and presents a schedule and cost-tracking sheet for an active project.
phases.milestoneShort: Certificate and a live project schedule

phases.title: Illinois broker's license
phases.split: 8–10 hours of pre-license coursework and exam prep, 2 on an algebra refresher
study: Illinois broker pre-license course, about 75 hours (requirements are set by IDFPR and change, so they are confirmed before the student enrolls)
State exam and license application
Khan Academy algebra refresher on the side
phases.milestone: Becomes a licensed Illinois broker, then tours and writes up three comparable properties.

phases.title: Finance, statistics and economics
phases.split: 5 hours of statistics and economics, 5 of MIT finance, 2–5 of pro forma modeling
study: Khan Academy: Statistics and Probability, Microeconomics, Macroeconomics
MIT OpenCourseWare 15.401, Finance Theory I
An Excel real estate pro forma (NOI, cap rates, IRR, debt service) built on one of the company's past deals
phases.milestone: Underwrites one deal independently and reviews it with the mentor.

phases.title: Software and prompt engineering
phases.split: 8–10 hours of software and prompt engineering, 4–5 of real estate learning mixed in
study: Harvard CS50 for programming fundamentals
Python for data work
Prompt engineering and AI tooling, used to build small tools: a deal analyzer, an RFI and daily-log helper for the field
Mixed in: construction finance and draw schedules, entitlement and permitting in Chicago, and reading real deal documents from company projects
phases.milestone: Ships one internal tool that the company actually uses.

phases.title: Network engineering and a development deal
phases.split: three months of networking alongside real estate law, leasing and market analysis, then four months on a development deal
study: Cisco Networking Academy or CompTIA Network+ prep, with hands-on work configuring the network for a building or the office
Mixed in: real estate law and contracts, property management and leasing, market analysis for Chicago neighborhoods, and shadowing the mentor in lender and investor meetings
Development deal: source, underwrite, schedule and pitch a small real development deal, with the mentor as the investor
phases.milestone: Delivers an investment memo for the deal and presents it.

phases.title: Capstone project
study: Works as the job site superintendent, managing a construction project
Takes on project management responsibilities as well: RFIs, submittals and the project paperwork normally expected from office support
phases.milestone: Manages a construction project as its superintendent while carrying the project management work.

threads.title: Law and zoning
threads.body: Real estate law and zoning basics every week: the Chicago zoning code and contracts.

threads.title: One book a month
threads.body: One development or finance book each month.

threads.title: Monthly check-in
threads.body: Fifteen minutes on progress, hours actually spent, and whether the pace needs to change.

how.title: Every lesson gets used on a real job
body: The program opens with six months of field support and closes with a year running a project. In the 30 months between, part-time work at 3F Construction is paired with part-time study, and the two are tied together: each course is matched to tasks on a project the company has under way.
During those 30 months the student works 30 hours a week and studies 10–15 more.

When the course covers critical path scheduling, the student finds the critical path on a project 3F Construction is building. When it covers construction loans, the student reads the term sheet for one of the company's loans and works out a month of interest.
The order is deliberate: early wins first, heavier academics later. Each phase ends with something the student has to produce and present to a mentor before the next one starts.

semester.title: The first coursework semester is planned to the day

threads.title: Three things that never stop
body: An hour or two a week, in every phase, goes to the same three habits.

family.title: The same frame would work for another family
body: Nothing about the structure is specific to real estate. It is phases, weeks, daily tasks and milestones, with every task tied to work the family business is already doing.
A family with a different trade could keep the frame and change the content: their own courses, their own jobs, their own milestones.
